claims.summary: The reference permits exact kNN for ordinary TOP plus distance ordering without APPROXIMATE, but separately requires APPROXIMATE when FORCE_ANN_ONLY is present. Q still has that hint, so this option incorrectly transfers the unforced behavior. It would match Q's exact strategy only after removing the forcing hint.

The no-index section documents kNN fallback for unforced search. The hint section requires an index when forcing ANN and states that missing either prerequisite fails the query. R could use the ordinary no-index fallback without the hint, not under its supplied forcing requirement.

The exact hint contract requires both the index and TOP WITH APPROXIMATE: P satisfies both, while Q and R each omit one. The latest-index optimizer may choose ANN or kNN when unforced, as in S. These are documented strategy classifications for stipulated valid trials, not executed plans or performance promises.

A compatible latest index does not force ANN by its existence; the current reference explicitly permits optimizer-selected kNN. S could happen to execute an ANN plan, but this is different from being forced to use that strategy. Adding the forcing hint would create a different trial.
